reader.requirement: At --std 85 a CLOSE naming several relative (or mixed) files must behave as one CLOSE per file-name-1 in written order: each file gets its own status, a failing one (42) does not stop the later ones, its USE procedure sees the earlier files already closed and the later ones untouched, and a WITH LOCK phrase applies only to its own file.

edition-consulted.switches: CLOSE WITH LOCK is admitted at 85 and refused at 2023 (COBOL0902, removed); the per-file decomposition is the same code

reader.edition-search: BindClose builds one BoundClose per file (BoundImplicitSeries) with no edition test; EmitClose and FileConnector.Close carry none (grep Edition/DialectLevel/DialectBehavior over SequentialIoBinder.cs, SequentialIoEmitter.cs EmitClose/EmitCloseScope, FileConnector.Close, CloseTable14.cs: only the VersionConformancePass WITH LOCK gate)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the decomposition and statuses are identical at 85 and 2023; only the WITH LOCK phrase's admission differs
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf18_05 covers order and per-file status across relative access modes and a sequential file; not the same file named twice, a failing file in the middle, or WITH LOCK on one file of several

probes.printed: CLOSE FA FA: USE-A 42 SB=99 SC=99, TWICE 42 / CLOSE FB FA FC: USE-A 42 SB=00 SC=99, MID 00 42 00
probes.expected: first FA closes, second FA is 42; FB closed before FA's 42 and FC closed after it

probes.printed: CLOSE FA FB WITH LOCK FC: LOCK 00 00 00; REOPEN-A 00; USE-B 38; REOPEN-B 38; REOPEN-C 00; at --std 2023 the program is refused COBOL0902 (WITH LOCK removed)
probes.expected: only FB is locked: OPEN of FB is 38 (VIII.1.3.4 GRL2.4d), FA and FC reopen 00

OK  §1985:VIII.1.3.4  (1.3.4 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.5b

reader.notes: The binder turns a multi-file CLOSE into a series of single-file implicit CLOSE statements, each emitted with its own status store and USE hook. The probe shows the order through what each USE procedure sees, and shows that a failure in the middle and a per-file WITH LOCK both behave as separate statements would.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-131/cl2.cob (runs/cl2-001, --std 85), no declaratives, mixed organizations (SR1): CLOSE FB FA FC FD1 with FA (relative) not open, FB indexed, FC sequential, FD1 relative sequential access: 'MIX 00 42 00 00', so the failing relative file in the middle neither stops the later files nor disturbs the earlier one and execution continues. CLOSE FD1 WITH LOCK FA FD1: FD1 locked then the second FD1 42, FA 00 ('LCK 42 00'); OPEN I-O FD1 then 38, OPEN I-O FA 00. Each is what separate CLOSE statements in written order give. The reader's edition site (VersionConformancePass WITH LOCK gate) is the only one; the per-file decomposition carries no edition test. cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.4.2.4 GR7 (the text is in GR7).
